- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.25) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; adjust upward to account for potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 65+), overshooting by 2–5% in next 3–5 days; apply dampening factor to peak forecasts.
- In 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price volatility; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.00–0.25) followed by a spike, model often fails to anticipate the rebound; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% in next 5–7 days.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends; if recent 5-day average is falling, add 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment to forecast.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is consistently low or negative, model underestimates true price; apply upward bias of 1–2% to compensate for sentiment-driven risk premium.
